title: A quasi-coherent module on a qcqs scheme is a directed colimit of modules of finite presentation (Stacks 01PK)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. An $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ is *of finite presentation* if every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U\to0$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules (Stacks, Modules, Definition 01BN). Then there exist a directed set $I$ (a nonempty preordered set in which any two elements have a common upper bound), a system $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i}:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_{i'})_{i\le i'}$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules of finite presentation over $I$ ($\varphi_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $\varphi_{i''i'}\circ\varphi_{i'i}=\varphi_{i''i}$), and $\mathcal O_X$-module maps $\varphi_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F$ with $\varphi_{i'}\circ\varphi_{i'i}=\varphi_i$, such that $(\mathcal F,(\varphi_i))$ is a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of the system in the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-filtered-colimit-finite-presentation] to obtain a small filtered category J, a diagram M of finite-presentation modules, and a colimit cocone c with vertex F. The qcqs and quasi-coherence hypotheses agree verbatim with those of the item.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-exists-directed-final], namely Mathlib CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.exists_directed, to J. Obtain a partial order I in the same universe, Nonempty I, IsDirected I (less than or equal), and a final functor G : I to J. Use the underlying preorder, set D = G composed with M, and select the original cocone legs at G.obj i. Every D.obj i has finite presentation by the corresponding property of M.obj (G.obj i). Functoriality and whiskered cocone naturality supply all system and compatibility equations.

The inverse of Mathlib Functor.Final.isColimitWhiskerEquiv G c sends the given colimit witness to one for c.whisker G. Its vertex is definitionally F and its natural transformation is the family chosen in the preceding step. Package this witness with I, its preorder, nonemptiness, directedness, D and the termwise finite-presentation witnesses. This is one application of the equivalence and the existential constructors, with no additional colimit-existence assumption.
